extracted.intended_audience: principal investigators, research institutions, small and large businesses, and other offerors preparing white papers or full proposals in response to ONR BAA N00014-23-S-B001
extracted.subtask_short: ONR BAA proposal & white paper preparation
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for preparing and submitting white papers and full proposals to ONR (BAA N00014-23-S-B001), including eligibility, required content and formatting, registration, security/classification, and evaluation criteria used to select awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key Dates / Submission Window
rubrics_metrics.description: This announcement will remain open for approximately one (1) year from the date of publication, or until replaced by a successor BAA. Proposals may be submitted at any time during this period. The Government reserves the right not to review proposals submitted after 30 September 2023, or after a successor to this Long Range BAA is issued, whichever occurs first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interested parties are urged to periodically check ONR, SAM.gov and Grants.gov for new BAA Calls and updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for Competition
rubrics_metrics.description: All responsible sources from academia, industry and the research community worldwide may submit proposals. HBCUs/MIs encouraged but no set-aside. FFRDCs and certain DoD/civilian labs and Navy laboratories, military universities and warfare centers are not eligible to receive awards under this BAA (team arrangements allowed where permitted). UARCs are eligible unless precluded by their DoD UARC contract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teaming is encouraged; offerors must be willing to cooperate and exchange software, data and other information in integrated programs. Disclosures of current and pending support may render an applicant ineligible; DoD may request ongoing updates that could discontinue funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contracted Fundamental Research Definition & Restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: ONR follows the USD (ATL) Memorandum definition of 'contracted fundamental research' (includes RDT&E Budget Activity 1; includes Budget Activity 2 when performed on-campus at a university). Research outside those bounds may be non-fundamental and subject to restrictions and DoD pre-publication review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offerors should consult Technical POCs to determine classification. If subcontractor work is unclassified fundamental research, the prime must identify and describe it in the proposal and confirm scoping/negotiation that it meets the definition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instrument Type & Characteristics (contract, grant, cooperative agreement, TIA, OTA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Awards may be contracts, grants, cooperative agreements, technology investment agreements (TIAs), and other transaction agreements (OTAs). Grants transfer value for public purpose with no fee and without substantial government involvement; cooperative agreements expect substantial involvement; TIAs and OTAs may involve cost share and are not duplicative of existing DoD programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TIAs/OTAs generally aim for ~50/50 cost share and no fee/profit; consult model contracts/grants links and relevant guidance (e.g., Other Transactions Guide) for instrument selection details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model Contracts and Governing Clauses
rubrics_metrics.description: Model contracts and grants are provided as examples on ONR websites; in event of conflict, current FAR, DFARS, NMCARS, or ONR clauses govern.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offerors should consult the linked examples but rely on current Federal Acquisition Regulation and agency clauses for governing terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost Sharing Policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost sharing is not expected under contracts and assistance awards and will not be used as a factor during merit review; the Government may consider voluntary cost sharing if proposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 2 CFR 200.306 and FAR 35.003 for additional guidance. OTAs may have cost sharing expectations (see Instrument Type entries).

rubrics_metrics.name: SAM Registration and Unique Entity Identifier Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All offerors submitting proposals or applications must be registered in SAM prior to submission, provide a valid unique entity identifier (UEI) in the application, and maintain an active SAM registration while an application or award is under consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Federal awarding agency may not make an award until SAM requirements are met; failure to comply can make an applicant ineligible. SAM may be accessed at https://sam.gov/content/home.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proprietary Marking & Non-Proprietary Statement of Work
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions protected per FAR 15.207; offerors are expected to mark pages that contain proprietary information. A non-proprietary version of the Statement of Work (SOW) must be submitted for all proposals. Do not put proprietary data/markings in or on the SOW.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If proposing restricted data, include the prescribed legend on the title page and mark each restricted sheet with the specified legend identifying the sheets to be restricted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security Classification and Classified Submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: White Papers and Proposals are expected to be unclassified, but classified white papers/proposals are permitted. If a classified proposal is submitted and selected for award, the resultant contract will be unclassified and must be accompanied by an unclassified SOW.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classified proposals must follow two-envelope submission instructions: outer envelope unclassified addressee (Document Control Unit), inner envelope stamped with overall classification and addressed to cognizant Technical POC.

rubrics_metrics.name: White Paper Format Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: White Paper formatting: 8.5 x 11-inch paper, 1-inch margins, single-spaced, Times New Roman 12 pt, page limit 5 pages excluding cover page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When email submission is required, white papers must be Microsoft Word 2016 or PDF compatible and email size limited to 5MB per email. FedConnect may be used as specified in the BAA Call.

rubrics_metrics.name: White Paper Mandatory Content
rubrics_metrics.description: White papers shall include: Cover Page (MANDATORY for ONR and ONRG) with Program Officer info; Technical Concept (technology innovation and technical risk areas); Future Naval Relevance; Operational Naval Concept (where applicable); Operational Utility Assessment Plan (where applicable); Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) cost estimate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FedConnect will not accept a white paper unless the Cover Sheet is included. Program Officer/Science Director info is required on the cover sheet; consult technology area pages for POC info.

rubrics_metrics.name: FedConnect Registration and Submission Procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: ONR utilizes FedConnect for white paper submission in applicable cases. Entities must register with SAM, obtain a UEI, and create a FedConnect account. First person registering needs a SAM MPIN.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FedConnect how-to guides and support contacts are provided; do not use FedConnect Message Center to submit questions—email the Section G POCs instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full Proposal Submission Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Full proposal requirements are provided in Appendix 1 for Grants/Cooperative Agreements/TIAs and Appendix 2 for Contracts and OTAs. White papers are often desired; consult the cognizant Program Officer regarding desirability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the appropriate Appendix instructions for the instrument type being pursued; ONR may request additional information after instrument determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation Criteria — Technical Merit & Responsiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall scientific and technical merits and responsiveness to the topic: degree of innovation; soundness of technical concept; Offeror's awareness of state of the art and scope of the problem; significance and originality of technical approach; anticipated scientific impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation also considers the Offeror’s capabilities, related experience, facilities, techniques or unique combinations integral to achieving objectives, and qualifications/experience of PI, team leader and key personnel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation Criteria — Naval Relevance & National Security Considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Potential naval relevance and contribution to ONR/DoN mission. Review will consider protection of IP, controlled information, key personnel and critical technologies; and may limit undue influence including foreign talent programs that might exploit U.S. technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consideration given to improper technology transfer, IP theft, cyber or human espionage, misleading information, concealed affiliations, or serious risk of improper technology transfer. NDAA-related restrictions (e.g., Confucius Institute rule) may apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation Criteria — Availability of Funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Availability of funds is a selection criterion (not applicable to white papers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criteria 1 (technical merit), 2 (naval relevance), and 3 (availability of funds) are equally important.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost Realism and Reasonableness Consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: To the extent appropriate, cost realism and reasonableness will be considered when selecting proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ONR reserves the right to request additional cost/pricing information and apply certified cost/pricing data rules where TINA thresholds are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review & Selection Process — Non-Comparative Review
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals will not be evaluated against each other since they are not submitted against a common work statement; ONR intends to review proposals as received though periodic administrative batching may occur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scientific/technical community makes recommendation; contracting and grants management performs cost analysis, responsibility determination, and fund confirmation. Recommendation is not a guarantee of award. ONR may remove offerors for failure to reach agreement on award terms or to provide required information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhanced Cybersecurity & CUI Controls Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: When applicable, certain offerors may be required to demonstrate compliance/ability to comply with enhanced cybersecurity requirements for unclassified networks housing Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI), in addition to DFARS 252.204-7012.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offerors are strongly encouraged to consult the cognizant Program Officer to determine whether enhanced controls will apply. See NMCARs 52.204.7303 and referenced NIST SP 800-171 DoD Assessment Requirements clauses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small Business Subcontracting Plan Requirement (> $750,000)
rubrics_metrics.description: For proposed contract awards exceeding $750,000, large businesses and non-profits must provide a Subcontracting Plan meeting FAR 19.704 and FAR 52.219-9 (supplemented by DFARS 252.219-7003). Small businesses are exempt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Plan is submitted as an attachment to the Proposal Checklist and not included in page count. Plans are reviewed for adequacy; failure to negotiate an acceptable Plan may make an apparent successful offeror ineligible for award. Offerors should propose realistic goals and provide explanations if SDB goals are below 5% or no positive goals are proposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subcontracting Resources & Encouragement of Small Business Participation
rubrics_metrics.description: ONR strongly commits to meaningful prime and subcontracting opportunities for various socioeconomic categories (SDBs, WOSBs, HUBZone, VOSBs, SDVOSBs, HBCUs/MIs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offerors may use listed resources (DSBS, SAM Contracting Opportunities, Navy SBIR/STTR search, SBA Subnet, USAspending.gov, DAU Small Business COP) to locate subcontracting partners and meet goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational Conflict of Interest (OCI) Disclosure & Certification
rubrics_metrics.description: Offerors must disclose any actual or potential OCI that may give an unfair competitive advantage, including: name of entity supported, contract/subcontract numbers, description of OCI, mitigation plan, and a signed certification statement disclosing all actual or potential OCIs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to disclose required information or make the certification will disqualify the offeror from consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: OCI Mitigation Plan Minimum Contents
rubrics_metrics.description: A Mitigation Plan must include organizational charts showing structure related to the OCI, demonstration of isolation of OCI-creating elements, geographic/physical separation info, personnel reassignment processes and restrictions, controls (e.g., NDAs) over future employment, OCI training details, and evidence supporting mitigation assertions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Contracting Officer will review certifications and mitigation plans and may require additional information; the Government may impose conditions, disqualify, award with mitigation, or seek a waiver. If accepted, the Mitigation Plan becomes contractually binding.

rubrics_metrics.name: TINA / Certified Cost or Pricing Data Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals submitted under this BAA that meet the Truth In Negotiations Act (TINA) threshold are subject to certified cost and pricing data and must execute the Certificate of Current Cost or Pricing Data as soon as practicable but no later than five business days after price agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Late submission of cost/pricing data after price agreement will be reviewed per FAR 15.407-1 to determine defectiveness and entitlement to price adjustment under FAR 52.215-10/11.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract Authority for Follow-on Production/Prototype Options
rubrics_metrics.description: Per statutory authority, a contract under this BAA may be awarded or modified to include CLINs or options for development/demonstration or initial/additional production of technology developed under the contract (10 USC 4004), and OTAs may allow follow-on production if prototype project completion and pre-included follow-on language criteria are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See NDAA and OTA statutory provisions for applicability and limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation & Disclosure Re: Covered Telecommunications (52.204-25)
rubrics_metrics.description: Offerors must comply with prohibitions on procuring or using covered telecommunications equipment or services (Section 889) and make required representations and disclosures about use/provision of such equipment or services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If responding 'will' or 'does' in specified representations, Offerors must provide detailed disclosure (OEM/entity info, model numbers, CAGE, description, proposed use, PSC codes where applicable) as part of the offer.

rubrics_metrics.name: List of Potential FAR/DFARS/NMCARS Clauses That May Apply
rubrics_metrics.description: The BAA lists numerous exemplary FAR/DFARS clauses that may be applicable to resulting awards (e.g., SAM, TRIC, cost/pricing, equal opportunity, trafficking in persons, cyber incident reporting, small business representations, restrictions related to China/PRC employment disclosures, prohibitions on foreign-made UAS, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ONR reserves the right to include any relevant and current FAR/DFARS/NMCARS/ONR clauses necessary in final awards based on dollar value; offerors should review cited clauses and be prepared to comply.
